title: Citizenship law in Ethiopia
competency: Examine how Ethiopian citizenship is acquired and lost, and the requirements for naturalization.

keywords.def: The law of a state that decides citizenship rights and responsibilities.
The fundamental law of a nation that guarantees civil rights and liberties.
A law issued by the government, like Proclamation No. 378/2003 on Ethiopian nationality.

en.text: Ethiopia made its first written citizenship law in 1930 G.C. Today the FDRE Constitution of 1995 G.C. sets the main ideas. Article 6 says a person with both or either Ethiopian parents is an Ethiopian citizen. So Ethiopia uses descent, or right of blood. Being born on Ethiopian land alone does not make you a citizen.

screens.title: How are you Ethiopian?
screens.ask: You are probably an Ethiopian citizen. How did you become one?
opts: Because one or both of my parents are Ethiopian
Because I bought an ID card
screens.after: Most Ethiopians are citizens by descent: their parents are Ethiopian. Read the law.

screens.title: 1.3 Citizenship law in Ethiopia
paras: Ethiopia enacted its first written citizenship law in 1930 G.C.
Before that, citizenship was mostly defined by custom and tradition.
The FDRE Constitution of 1995 G.C. gives the main ideas about citizenship today.

screens.title: Article 6 of the FDRE Constitution
paras: Any person of either gender who has both or either Ethiopian parents is an Ethiopian citizen.
So the Constitution recognises citizenship by descent, or blood.
Proclamation No. 378/2003 gives the details of Ethiopian nationality.
In Ethiopia there is no broad right to citizenship by birthplace on the land.

opts: Any person with both or either Ethiopian parents
Only people with two Ethiopian parents
Anyone who lives in Addis Ababa
screens.ans: Any person with both or either Ethiopian parents
screens.why: Article 6: both or either Ethiopian parents is enough.
screens.clue: Does it need one parent or two?

screens.text: Ethiopia enacted its first written citizenship law in 1930 G.C.
Which principle does the FDRE Constitution use for Ethiopian citizenship?
screens.why: Ethiopian nationality is inherited mainly by descent.
screens.clue: Is it about parents or about land?

screens.text: An Ethiopian mother and an American father have a baby in France. Under Ethiopian law, is the baby Ethiopian?
opts: No, the baby was born in France
Yes, by descent through the Ethiopian mother
Only if the baby moves to Ethiopia at 18
screens.ans: Yes, by descent through the Ethiopian mother
screens.why: Article 6 needs only either parent to be Ethiopian. Place of birth does not matter for descent.
screens.clue: Does Article 6 need one Ethiopian parent or two? Does the birthplace matter?

ideas.name: Naturalization and loss in Ethiopian law

en.text: A foreigner can become Ethiopian by naturalization if he meets eight requirements. For example, he must be an adult, have lived in Ethiopia for at least four years and speak one of the country's languages. In exceptional cases, a foreigner who made a great contribution may be granted citizenship. Under Ethiopian law, no Ethiopian can lose citizenship against his or her will.

screens.title: One month in Ethiopia
screens.ask: A foreigner has lived in Ethiopia for one month. Can he apply for Ethiopian citizenship now?
opts: No, he must have lived here at least four years
screens.after: Proclamation No. 378/2003 asks for at least four years of living in Ethiopia, plus other requirements.

screens.title: Requirements for naturalization
paras: Proclamation No. 378/2003 also allows naturalization after birth.
A foreigner seeking Ethiopian nationality must meet these requirements:
table: be an adult and legally capable under Ethiopian law
live in Ethiopia for a total of at least four years before applying
be able to speak any language of the nations/nationalities of the country
have enough lawful income to support himself and his family
be a person of good character
be released from the previous nationality, or be stateless

screens.title: Exceptional cases and loss
paras: In exceptional cases, a foreigner who made a significant contribution to Ethiopia may be granted citizenship.
No Ethiopian may be stripped of citizenship by a government decision.
Citizenship is lost only if the person renounces it, or freely takes another nationality.
Article 33(1): no Ethiopian may lose citizenship against his or her will.
screens.note: So under Ethiopian law, involuntary loss of citizenship is not permitted.

screens.text: A foreign doctor has worked in Ethiopia for two years and saved many lives. The government wants to honour her with citizenship. Is this possible?
opts: No, she has not lived here four years
Yes, in exceptional cases, for a significant contribution
Only if she marries an Ethiopian
No, foreigners can never become Ethiopian
screens.ans: Yes, in exceptional cases, for a significant contribution
screens.why: The Proclamation allows citizenship in exceptional cases for people who made a significant contribution, regardless of the usual requirements.
screens.clue: Read the Remember box about special recognition.

items.text: An Ethiopian mother and an American father have a child in France. Under Ethiopian law, what is the baby's citizenship?
items.why: Article 6: either Ethiopian parent is enough.
items.clue: Does the birthplace matter under Ethiopian law?

items.text: How can this newborn become an Ethiopian citizen?
opts: By descent (right of blood) through the Ethiopian mother
items.ans: By descent (right of blood) through the Ethiopian mother
items.why: Ethiopia uses right of blood, and one Ethiopian parent is enough.

test.text: Which law of 1995 G.C. sets the main ideas of Ethiopian citizenship today?
A child with only one Ethiopian parent can be an Ethiopian citizen.
test.why: Article 6: both or either Ethiopian parents.

test.text: Which proclamation gives the details of Ethiopian nationality?
How can an Ethiopian lose citizenship under Ethiopian law?
opts: Only by giving it up voluntarily or freely taking another nationality
By a government decision against his will
test.ans: Only by giving it up voluntarily or freely taking another nationality

test.text: A foreigner aged 30 has lived in Ethiopia for 5 years, speaks Afaan Oromoo, has a job and no criminal record. What else must he do?
opts: Be released from his old nationality (or be stateless) and take the oath of allegiance
test.ans: Be released from his old nationality (or be stateless) and take the oath of allegiance
test.why: Requirements vii and viii are still needed (and good character).
